title: Method for full protein sequence mapping: LC-MS sample preparation
protocol: Denature protein samples prior to protease digestion.
Treat the denatured protein with DTT to break disulfide linkages between cysteine residues.
Modify reactive cysteine -SH groups with iodoacetamide to prevent disulfide bond reformation.
Digest proteins using endoproteinase Lys-C to cleave on the c-terminal side of lysine.
Digest proteins using trypsin to cleave on the c-terminal side of lysine and arginine amino acids.
Since maximal amino acid coverage of the protein is required, it is best to digest the sample with several proteases.
Determine the appropriate cleavage sites for Glu-C protease on the c-terminal side of glutamic acid and aspartic acid residues.
Select chymotrypsin protease to cleave specifically on the c-terminal side of tyrosine, phenylalanine, and tryptophan amino acids.
Consider that chymotrypsin will less frequently act on leucine, methionine, alanine, aspartic acid, and glutamic acid residues.
Choose proteases to yield peptides from 600-6000 Da.
Maximize the coverage of potential phosphorylation sites in the protein.
